skill.name: find-replace
skill.description: Use sd with rg, fd, and git workflows to preview and apply find-and-replace changes across codebases.
skill.summary: Guides safe text replacement, regex matching, and batch edits with the sd command-line tool.
skill.author: 0xDarkMatter

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline command examples, or benign regex guidance. I confirmed the unquoted command-substitution workflows and the .env replacement example because they can affect sensitive files or mis-handle unsafe filenames. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration intent, or hidden malicious behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Unquoted command substitution is used to pass file lists into sd.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer fd -x, xargs -0, or another null-delimited workflow, and quote every path passed to sd.

remediation.issue: The advanced configuration example edits .env* files.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit warning and require user confirmation before changing environment files or secret-bearing configuration.

remediation.issue: The Docker example mounts the workspace and runs sh -c inside a container.
remediation.suggestion: Mark the Docker workflow as optional, require confirmation, and pin any image or package versions used in examples.

content.value_statement: Large codebases make repeated text changes slow and error-prone. This skill guides sd-based replacements with previews, regex patterns, and batch workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains basic sd syntax for replacing text in one file or many files.
Shows how to preview replacements before writing changes.
Maps common sed commands to simpler sd equivalents.
Documents regex capture groups, word boundaries, and escaping rules.
Provides batch workflows using rg, fd, git file lists, and Docker examples.
Includes examples for imports, API paths, configuration keys, and React files.
limitations: Requires the sd command-line tool to be installed and available in the shell.
In-place replacements can damage files when patterns are too broad.
Regex accuracy depends on the user-supplied search and replacement patterns.
Rollback is not automated beyond normal git review and restore workflows.

use_cases.title: Rename Symbols Across a Project
use_cases.description: Replace old variable, function, or component names while previewing affected files first.

use_cases.title: Update Imports During Refactors
use_cases.description: Convert relative imports, reorganize named imports, or change module paths across TypeScript files.

use_cases.title: Modernize Repeated Text Patterns
use_cases.description: Apply repeatable replacements for API paths, configuration names, logging calls, and JSX attributes.

prompt_templates.title: Preview a Simple Replacement
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner replacement in one area of a project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the find-replace skill to preview replacing oldName with newName under src. Do not modify files yet.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Reviewed Replacement
prompt_templates.scenario: User has reviewed the preview and wants a controlled edit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use sd to replace oldName with newName in matching TypeScript files. Show the changed files and summarize the diff.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Import Paths
prompt_templates.scenario: Project import paths need a consistent alias.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find imports that use ../utils and replace them with @/utils. Preview matches first, then apply only after confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Batch Migration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced multi-step migration with several patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a safe batch replacement plan for renaming oldApi methods to newApi methods. Include preview, apply, verify, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Preview replacing a deprecated function name across source files.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists likely matches, explains the replacement scope, and asks before applying in-place edits.

output_examples.input: Change import paths from a relative utility folder to a project alias.
output_examples.output: The assistant previews affected import statements, applies the replacement after approval, and summarizes changed files.

output_examples.input: Plan several API method renames during a migration.
output_examples.output: The assistant groups replacements by method, recommends a safe execution order, and includes verification with search and diff review.

best_practices: Preview every replacement before modifying files.
Use narrow paths and word boundaries to avoid unintended matches.
Review git diff after each batch before starting another batch.
anti_patterns: Do not run broad replacements across the repository without a preview.
Do not edit secret-bearing files unless the user explicitly requests it.
Do not rely on unquoted shell-expanded file lists for unknown repositories.

faq.question: What tool does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses sd, a command-line replacement tool designed to be simpler than sed for many common edits.

faq.question: Does it modify files automatically?
faq.answer: The examples include in-place edits, but a safe workflow previews matches and asks before applying changes.

faq.question: Can it replace text across many files?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows batch workflows with rg, fd, git file lists, and scoped glob patterns.

faq.question: Can it handle regular expressions?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents capture groups, word boundaries, multiline patterns, and escaping for special characters.

faq.question: Is this a full refactoring engine?
faq.answer: No. It performs text and regex replacement, so users must verify syntax and behavior after changes.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
